[untitled BTM module] These genes read as the secretory programme of a mesenchymal stromal or fibroblast-like cell that builds and maintains tissue architecture and supports the cells embedded in it. CXCL12 is the chemokine by which such stroma recruits and retains haematopoietic progenitors and lymphocytes, while IGF1 with its carrier IGFBP3 sets local growth-factor availability, FRZB tunes Wnt signalling as a secreted antagonist, and complement component C7 and the secreted nuclease DNASE1L3 contribute to clearance of extracellular debris and immune tone.

[untitled BTM module] These genes sketch a morphogen-driven programme that patterns mesenchymal tissue and steers progenitors toward bone, cartilage, skin and blood-supporting fates. BMP signalling sits at its centre: SMAD1 carries the receptor signal to the nucleus, ZNF521 acts as a nuclear cofactor tuning that output in skeletal and haematopoietic progenitors, while secreted GREM1 antagonises BMP ligands to keep niches permissive, and INHBA contributes an activin/TGF-beta arm through its own receptor-SMAD route.

[untitled BTM module] A small, mixed regulatory collection whose centre of gravity is the decision between proliferation, growth arrest and death. The PI3K catalytic subunit p110delta and the forkhead factor FOXO4 sit on opposite ends of one axis: signalling through phosphoinositide 3-kinase keeps FOXO factors out of the nucleus, and when that signal weakens FOXO-driven transcription pushes cells toward quiescence, stress resistance and apoptosis.
